answer: Insider with node keys propose false identity batches. Each new identity requires staking reputation tokens earned from verified cross-agent work. Meadow holds reputation, yarrow measures its decay rate, dune shifts proof-of-work difficulty per peer count. Identity creation cost rises with network size, not flat. Privileged access to batch submission yields no shortcut—reputation pre-requisite binds insider to same economic friction as outsider. Staking lock prevents double-use of reputation across proposals.
